page: Amazon Web Services g6e.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. The system is provisioned with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7R13 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 128 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering an 8 GB per-core allocation. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA L40S GPU built on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 45 GB of VRAM. High-speed local scratch storage is integrated via a 600 GB NVMe SSD, complemented by a 20 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark evaluations reveal that the instance delivers exceptional throughput in artificial intelligence workloads. Large language model inference achieves top-tier results across small, medium, and large architectures, demonstrated by prompt processing throughputs reaching 13,568.43 tokens per second on 135M parameter models and 885.42 tokens per second on 70B models. Single-core CPU computation ranks within the top 25 percent in stress-ng testing at 2,992.45 points, while general multi-core compute, Geekbench ratings, and PassMark scores land in the middle tier.

The primary architectural tradeoff lies in system memory bus saturation. While small-block cached memory bandwidth is resilient, uncached large-block sequential read and write memory bandwidth fell into the lower quartile, recording 38.63 GB/s and 22.82 GB/s respectively. Consequently, tasks requiring extreme memory bandwidth independent of the GPU may encounter bottlenecks. However, with dedicated vCPU allocations, balanced local NVMe performance, and modern GPU acceleration, the hardware profile offers strong compute and memory density without requiring clusters of larger multi-GPU hosts.

The configuration makes Amazon Web Services g6e.4xlarge well suited for generative AI inference, medium-scale model fine-tuning, ray tracing, 3D graphics rendering, and video processing pipelines requiring rapid local scratch space and modern tensor execution.
description: Amazon Web Services g6e.4xlarge is an accelerated computing instance configured with an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor offering 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores) at 3.4 GHz, 128 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 600 GB local NVMe SSD. Accelerated workloads leverage an NVIDIA L40S GPU with 45 GB of VRAM. Benchmark results position the server in the top tier for LLM inference across 135M, 7B, and 70B parameter models, alongside upper-quartile single-core CPU execution. System memory bandwidth shows lower-tier throughput during large-block uncached read and write passes, indicating optimal cost-to-performance efficiency when workflows maximize GPU tensor operations rather than system memory streaming. Supported by a 20 Gbps network baseline, this instance is suited for AI inference, 3D rendering, and graphics-intensive computing.
